bull.b: The 35% year-to-date revenue increase shows that Cibus is beginning to convert its technology and collaboration programs into commercial sales. Continued growth in sustainable ingredients could diversify revenue beyond future crop-trait royalties and provide an early foundation for broader commercialization.

Favorable regulatory treatment across multiple jurisdictions reduces a major commercialization barrier for gene-edited traits and supports progress toward market launches. These decisions strengthen the platform’s applicability across crops, although local implementation and launch execution will still determine the timing of benefits.

Lower R&D and SG&A spending demonstrates that management has implemented meaningful cost controls while continuing to advance the platform. Sustained discipline can extend available resources, reduce the rate of cash consumption, and improve operating leverage if commercial revenue expands over time.

bear.b: The projected runway into only early Q1 2027 leaves limited financial flexibility relative to the time needed to commercialize crop traits. Continued cash usage may require additional financing before larger royalties arrive, potentially diverting resources from development and commercialization priorities.

Cibus remains far from breakeven despite revenue growth and narrower losses, because its revenue base is still small relative to operating costs. Persistent losses and negative cash flow weaken financial resilience and make the business dependent on future funding or successful commercialization to support operations.

Cibus does not control the full path from trait development to commercial sales, since partner validation, production, pricing, orders, and crop adoption must occur first. This dependency delays cash realization and makes the timing and scale of future licensing and royalty revenue less certain.
